Summary: Migrate document processing pipeline from Databricks to OpenShift
Description:
The document processing logic currently runs as a Databricks job that monitors an ADLS Gen2 landing folder, processes new files, and writes results back to ADLS for user download. The frontend and backend already run on OpenShift.

This epic moves the processing logic into a single-replica, always-on Python worker on OpenShift that processes files SERIALLY, driven by a job table in Azure SQL. There is no Spark dependency and daily volume is a few dozen files, so one pod is sufficient.

Serial processing in a single pod is also the throttling strategy: the internal LLM gateway enforces a per-minute token limit, and one in-flight request at a time keeps us under it without any distributed rate limiter.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (deliberate - do not add back): message queue, distributed rate limiting, horizontal autoscaling, per-file Kubernetes Jobs.

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- All new uploads processed by the OpenShift worker, output byte-identical to Databricks.
- Multi-file uploads drain in order without triggering LLM gateway rate limits.
- Databricks job disabled; rollback possible within 1 hour for 30 days after cutover.

Create processing_job table and claim semantics in Azure SQL
Description:
The job table replaces both the folder-monitoring trigger and a message queue. The backend inserts a row on upload; the worker polls for QUEUED rows and claims them atomically.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- processing_job table created with migration script under version control.
- Worker can claim a job atomically; no double-claim on restart or overlapping polls.
- Stale RUNNING rows left by a crashed pod are recovered automatically.

Implement the serial worker main loop
Description:
The worker polls the job table, processes one file at a time, records state transitions, and writes output back to the existing ADLS output path.

Serial execution is intentional and load-bearing: it is what keeps us inside the LLM gateway's per-minute token limit. Do not introduce a thread pool or asyncio concurrency here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Files processed one at a time with status recorded at each transition.
- Output path convention identical to the Databricks job.
- SIGTERM never loses a file.

Create OpenShift deployment manifests
Description:
Deploy the worker as a single replica with no autoscaling. Replica count is a correctness constraint, not a capacity decision: additional replicas would run LLM calls in parallel and breach the gateway's token limit.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Worker deployed to preprod at replicas: 1 with no HPA or KEDA configured.
- Rollout strategy prevents old and new pods running simultaneously.
- Outbound connectivity through the corporate proxy verified.
